commitResults.messageTitle: Show the displayed client count in the footer

visible list after commands. Cover additions, deletions, searches,
list restoration and clearing in the UI test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Set the minimum window size to 820 by 440

The window minimum is too narrow for two panes and too tall for
smaller screens at 150 percent scaling.

Set the minimum width to 820 and height to 440 so both panes have
room while the window can fit shorter screens.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a prompt in the empty detail panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail placeholder is blank and gives no guidance about its
purpose. Users need a clear indication of what belongs in that space.

Show a selection prompt to explain the purpose of the detail pane.
Keep the message readable within the available space.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Focus the command box when the app opens
commitResults.messageBody:
The expanded window introduces additional focusable controls.
Users should be able to start typing commands immediately.

Focus the command input after the window has finished loading so
users can begin without clicking the field. Add a startup UI test
to guard this behaviour.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the main window at supported layout sizes
commitResults.messageBody:
The two-pane window must remain usable when display scaling
reduces the available space. Layout changes could otherwise hide
controls or overlap the footer.

Add an automated check for the effective layout sizes in issue #88
and the minimum window size. Verify that the main regions fit,
pane widths are preserved, and footer labels do not overlap.

These checks simulate available layout space rather than native
operating-system display scaling.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Restructure client cards into three rows
commitResults.messageBody:
Client cards spread contact details across several lines and repeat
the address, making the list harder to scan.

Group the index, name and role above a shared phone and email row,
with tags underneath. Remove the address from the card without
changing stored client data.

Constrain long name and email text so role badges remain visible
in narrow lists. Add UI tests for the field layout and text overflow.

Refs #95

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep client cards at a consistent compact height
commitResults.messageBody:
Cards shrink when tags are absent and grow when tags wrap, so the
list cannot maintain a predictable density on small screens.

Keep the base card height at 70 pixels and fit tags on one row.
Show a count and tooltip for tags that do not fit, restoring tags
as more space becomes available.

Add tests for optional fields, tag overflow, layout stability and
three complete cards in a compact list. These are layout checks,
not native operating-system display-scaling verification.

Refs #95

commitResults.messageTitle: Use singular wording for one displayed client
commitResults.messageBody:
The footer uses a plural label even when only one client is displayed.
This produces the grammatical error '1 clients' during normal use.

Show '1 client' for a count of one and retain 'clients' for all other
counts. Update the add, find and delete UI checks to guard the wording.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master and address main window review
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window branch conflicts with the merged clear-confirmation
tests. Its layout test also implies display-scaling coverage that it
does not provide.

The branch needs the latest team changes without losing either set of
tests or claiming unverified display-scaling results.

Merge master while preserving both sets of tests. Require confirmation
before checking an empty footer, assert the placeholder text, and add
manual display-scaling instructions with results left unverified.

Refs #88

These unused rules suggest that CSS controls spacing even though

Remove the obsolete gap rules while retaining the tag-label styles

Refs #95

commitResults.messageTitle: Show labelled requirements on client cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Client cards omit requirements, making price and property preferences
harder to compare at a glance.

Add an optional summary below the tags with labelled prices, sorted
areas and housing types. Omit missing values, use middle-dot separators
and truncate long summaries without wrapping.

Keep cards at 70 pixels without requirements and 90 pixels with them.
Add regression tests for summary formatting, visibility and layout.

Refs #98

commitResults.messageTitle: Record Windows display-scaling test results
commitResults.messageBody:
The testing guide still lists actual display scaling as unverified.
Teammate checks now cover all three configurations on Windows 11.

Record passing results for the original PR #112 build and link the
test report and screenshots. Align the checklist with opening and
maximised layouts, footer updates and Help-window checks.

Scope the results to commit 4c0c4e47 and require repeat checks after
later UI changes so the record does not imply untested builds pass.

Refs #123

commitResults.messageTitle: Size client cards from their content
commitResults.messageBody:
Fixed card and row heights can clip larger fonts while layout tests
still pass because they only check the capped bounds.

Let cards and rows grow with their text, retain compact default
spacing, and reserve the selection border to keep card sizes stable.

Add font-metric and compact-window tests to check requirement cards,
selection stability, and scrolling to the final card.

Refs #98

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle platform font metrics in client cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Platform-dependent font metrics make exact height assertions brittle
and can push requirement cards past their compact height budget.

Reduce vertical padding while preserving content-driven growth.
Validate text metrics, row containment and viewport fit, retaining
the 90-pixel default-font limit and checks for overlap and clipping.

Exercise available font families, including Segoe UI when installed,
and verify that missing tags do not change a card's height.

Refs #98

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct content-sized card layout assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
The replacement-font test applies the default 90-pixel limit to fonts
that can require more space. It fails on Windows even when all rows
fit. Comparing the card with its own preferred height also repeats
the size assigned by the test setup.

Keep content-fit checks for replacement fonts and compare card
height with laid-out content plus vertical insets. Remove the unused
FXML injection id while retaining the CSS and test lookup id.

Refs #98

commitResults.messageTitle: Style the client interface consistently
commitResults.messageBody:
The master-detail layout still uses mismatched legacy colours and
inconsistent styling across client cards and the profile panel.

Apply a shared charcoal palette, rounded cards, readable labels and
clear selection without hiding role badges. Keep content-driven
card heights and the existing Buyer, Seller wording.

Add rendered-style tests for badge colours, text contrast and stable
selection sizing. Track actual display-scale verification in #134.

Refs #102

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep three client cards visible in short windows
commitResults.messageBody:
Window decorations reduce the usable height below the viewport used
by the original tests, leaving the third requirement card clipped.

Select a compact layout from the content height. Reduce result-area
height and surrounding padding without shrinking text, and restore
the normal layout when the window grows. Keep feedback scrollable.

Add regression checks for three complete requirement cards, control
containment, feedback readability and restoration after resizing.
Actual operating-system display-scale verification remains in #134.

Refs #102, #134

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep client cards compact across platform fonts
commitResults.messageBody:
Windows system font metrics can make requirement cards exceed the
90-pixel budget and clip the third card in short windows.

Use Arial for card typography and tighten row and badge spacing
without reducing text sizes or capping content-driven heights.

Add a regression test that changes the surrounding window font while
checking stable card fonts, compact height and unclipped content.

Refs #102

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore native fonts on client cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Forcing Arial can make small card text look smeared on macOS.
Fixed pixel-height assertions also assume identical font metrics
across operating systems.

Let cards inherit the native window font and recover space by
reducing vertical padding without shrinking text. Keep card heights
content-driven and retain the three-complete-cards viewport check.

Check font inheritance and actual text containment instead of a
fixed 90-pixel height limit.

Refs #102

commitResults.messageBody: Style the interface and adapt it to short windows

commitResults.messageBody: Add model history integration and undoable command metadata

commitResults.messageTitle: Add history menu actions and shortcuts
commitResults.messageBody:
The history commands need menu and keyboard access.

Route each action through the command box and retain unfinished text.

Test menu clicks and platform shortcuts, including command-box focus.

Refs #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Document undo and redo in User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need the command syntax and limits before using history.

Document undoable changes and the 20-change limit.

Explain redo invalidation and session-only history.

Refs #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Add transactional undo and redo commands
commitResults.messageBody:
History controls need typed commands and reliable saves before users
can reverse client changes safely.

Add undo, redo, and history feedback, record mutations only after a
successful save, and restore data and stacks if saving fails. Replace
the data file atomically so a failed write preserves the last saved
version. Cover parsing and failure paths with tests.

Refs #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Test undo and redo across all mutations
commitResults.messageBody:
Undo and redo affect six mutation commands, but their end-to-end
persistence and redo invalidation need explicit coverage.

Exercise each mutation through save, undo, and redo against the data
file. Check multi-step history order and redo invalidation after a new
change.

Refs #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Document undo and redo persistence flow
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide does not explain how snapshots become saved
history or how failed saves preserve client data and stack order.

Document model ownership, normal command execution, undo and redo
transfers, and atomic file replacement so maintainers can reason
about failure recovery.

Refs #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover history shortcut and rollback paths
commitResults.messageBody:
Codecov reports patch coverage below its target because rejected
keyboard shortcuts and failed history rollback are untested.

Cover non-history key combinations and make rollback failure
explicit after a save error.

Refs #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover redo accelerator and shortcut branches
commitResults.messageBody:
Patch coverage misses the alternate redo accelerator and a
redundant shift branch. Make the platform choice testable on every
CI system and remove the redundant check without changing behavior.

Refs #133

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify history actions during pending clear
commitResults.messageBody:
